FORCING FUNCTIONS AND PRAGMA. This TU compiles under `#pragma defer_codegen off` and carries two uncalled functions, dPathLiftActor_c_EmitDeletingDestructor and dPathLiftActor_c_EmitDestructor, recorded as compiler_only_output deadstrip rows. The destructor itself stays inline in include/dPathLiftActor_c.h because the class's descendants inline its vptr store.

compiler_only_output.reason: Not called and not in the ROM: a source-level forcing function. The class destructor is defined inline in its header because the descendants inline its vptr store, so no file can define it out of line; a delete-expression asks for the deleting variant by name. This file compiles under `#pragma defer_codegen off`, where ordinary functions are emitted at parse time in source order -- the only measured lever that makes mwccarm emit D0 before D1 as the cartridge has them -- and this forcer is the parse-time trigger that places D0 first. Emitted between the licensed D0 and D1 sections. Homeless: config/ has no symbol row for it.

Not called and not in the ROM: the companion forcing function. An explicit `p->~dPathLiftActor_c()` asks for the complete-object variant by name; the delete-expression forcer cannot serve both, because a plain destructor call alone does not reproduce the deleting variant out of line. This file compiles under `#pragma defer_codegen off`, where ordinary functions are emitted at parse time in source order, so the call places D1 after D0 as the cartridge has them. Emitted between the licensed D1 section and the first real member, so it does not disturb the licensed run. Homeless: config/ has no symbol row for it.
